title: Institutional FX Dashboard & Intelligence Report — July 13, 2026

regime.classification: Event-Driven, tilting Risk-Off — the Iran/Strait of Hormuz crisis escalated sharply over the weekend from a declared-over ceasefire to a formal Iranian closure of the Strait and a US naval blockade, and today's market reaction is more clearly risk-off than any prior session in this crisis.
regime.justification: VIX jumped intraday to ~16.39 (+9.05% vs Friday's ~15.03 close), and US cash equities fell broadly (Dow -0.2%, S&P 500 -0.7%, Nasdaq -1.4% on renewed AI-stock pressure) rather than shrugging off the news as in prior sessions. The US 10Y yield holds at 4.58% (little changed from Thursday's 4.59%), and oil extended its rally sharply (Brent surging as much as 4.2-7.1% on different measures to the $79-81 area).
regime.executiveSummary: The single biggest cross-asset driver is a major weekend escalation in the Iran/Strait of Hormuz crisis: Iran formally announced it had closed the Strait of Hormuz "until further notice," President Trump responded by announcing the US would reinstate a naval blockade of Iranian ships and begin charging a 20% toll on all cargo transiting the waterway, and Iran retaliated with strikes against US allies Kuwait, Jordan, and Qatar — the fourth US strike on Iran in a week followed an Iranian attack on a Cyprus-flagged container ship. Shipping through the Strait has fallen roughly 52% week-on-week. Oil has surged further on the news (Brent briefly topping $81, WTI in the $72-75 range), while gold has continued to fall (~$4,064-4,107/oz) in the same "safe-haven paradox" this crisis has produced since last week. Markets now turn to Tuesday's US June CPI print and a slate of major bank earnings (JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo) — the Fed's (US Federal Reserve's) next real data test after last Wednesday's hawkish June minutes. USD/JPY remains near its weakest yen level in roughly four decades, still without any safe-haven bid despite the worst escalation of this crisis yet.

excluded.reasoning: Explicitly considered and excluded for a third consecutive report. The move (Brent to the $79-81 area) is real and remains this report's biggest single ongoing data point, and the situation has only escalated further — a formal Strait closure, a US naval blockade with a 20% toll, and a multi-country Iranian retaliation cycle (Kuwait, Jordan, Qatar) all developed over the weekend. Iran is also reportedly continuing separate talks with Oman on safe passage, meaning the situation could still move sharply toward de-escalation as well as further escalation within days. Building a precise entry/target/stop around a shock this fluid still doesn't meet this report's bar for a leveled, verifiable idea; this remains better captured in Section 10's scenario framing.

contrarianCheck.primaryRisk: The Iran/Hormuz situation could still move sharply in either direction — reports that Iran is pursuing parallel talks with Oman on safe passage suggest a swift de-escalation remains possible even after this weekend's severe escalation, which would likely reverse the oil rally and unwind some of the safe-haven-dollar bid. Separately, USD/JPY's now four-plus-session failure to respond to an escalating crisis is itself becoming the report's central risk to monitor — a delayed, abrupt safe-haven catch-up move (or an intervention headline) remains a live tail risk that would move sharply against the short thesis's timing even if not its direction.
contrarianCheck.invalidationFactor: A confirmed de-escalation headline on Iran/Hormuz — even a partial one, such as concrete progress in the Iran-Oman safe-passage talks — combined with a soft US CPI print Tuesday would be the cleanest scenario to reverse the current broad-dollar strength and reduce oil's safe-haven premium.
contrarianCheck.bullCase: NZD/USD extends toward its second target (0.5820); AUD/NZD's stalled pullback resumes toward 1.1950 as the RBNZ/China-CPI theses continue to work; BoJ/MOF rhetoric hardens further or an actual intervention lands, cooling USD/JPY. keyThemes: The Iran/Strait of Hormuz crisis escalated sharply over the weekend from a "ceasefire is over" declaration to a formal Iranian closure of the Strait and a US naval blockade with a 20% cargo toll. Iran retaliated with strikes against Kuwait, Jordan, and Qatar; shipping through the Strait has fallen roughly 52% week-on-week; oil has surged further (Brent briefly above $81).

NZD/USD has cleared its first published target, the clearest confirmed win in this report's tracker so far , as the RBNZ's (New Zealand) 8 Jul hike continues to prove a durable, multi-session catalyst even against a broad-dollar-strength crosscurrent.

USD/JPY's now four-plus-session failure to catch any safe-haven bid — even through a formal Strait closure and naval blockade — remains this crisis's single most striking cross-asset anomaly , and the item most likely to produce an abrupt catch-up move if the market's read on it changes, with tomorrow's US CPI and bank earnings adding fresh two-way risk into the pair.

VIX shows a genuine cross-source conflict this session (an intraday spike to ~16.39, +9.05%, vs. a separate read of 15.34, -3.16%) — both are surfaced in Section 8, with the higher, spike figure used for the regime classification given its consistency with today's broader risk-off equity tone; confirm the true closing print at the next run.

Brent crude shows a similarly wide same-day conflict ($79.22, +4.2% vs. $81.40, +7.1%, depending on whether the toll/blockade announcement is reflected) — both surfaced rather than arbitrarily resolved; pin down the confirmed close at the next run.

Nikkei 225, DAX, and FTSE 100 precise closing index levels (not just % moves) could not be independently confirmed at compilation time this session — only percentage changes were available; pin down exact levels at the next run.

Global Equity Leaderboard: KOSPI's YTD %, DAX's YTD conflict, and Sensex's YTD/12-month conflict (all flagged across multiple prior reports) remain unresolved this session — none were re-investigated given time constraints; prioritize at least one of these at the next run.

The Long NZD/USD idea (Sections 2/6) has now cleared its first published target (0.5750) — the next run should formally treat this as resolved/substantially de-risked in its write-up rather than continuing to carry it as an undifferentiated "still pending" alongside the other three ideas, and should watch specifically for a close above the second target (0.5820) or a reversal.

The Short USD/JPY idea (Section 9) has fallen below the halfway confidence mark (49/100) for the first time — worth an explicit discussion at the next run about whether this idea should be retired/replaced given three consecutive sessions of deterioration, even though it has not technically hit its stop.

This is the sixth run of the merged structure (first run: 4 Jul 2026; second: 6 Jul 2026; third: 7 Jul 2026; fourth: 8 Jul 2026; fifth: 9 Jul 2026; note 5 Jul and 10-12 Jul 2026 were not run under this structure) — Section 2, hit-rate tracker, and Section 9/15 deltas continue to build a genuine multi-report baseline despite the gap.

- *Positioning Layer:* No fresh CFTC read confirmed this session; the "near-record bearish (short-yen)" characterization grows more stale each session.

sections.title: Contrarian Check & Risks
sections.raw:
**Primary thesis risk:** The Iran/Hormuz situation could still move sharply in either direction — reports that Iran is pursuing parallel talks with Oman on safe passage suggest a swift de-escalation remains possible even after this weekend's severe escalation, which would likely reverse the oil rally and unwind some of the safe-haven-dollar bid. Separately, USD/JPY's now four-plus-session failure to respond to an escalating crisis is itself becoming the report's central risk to monitor — a delayed, abrupt safe-haven catch-up move (or an intervention headline) remains a live tail risk that would move sharply against the short thesis's timing even if not its direction.

**Overall-view invalidation factor:** A confirmed de-escalation headline on Iran/Hormuz — even a partial one, such as concrete progress in the Iran-Oman safe-passage talks — combined with a soft US CPI print Tuesday would be the cleanest scenario to reverse the current broad-dollar strength and reduce oil's safe-haven premium.

- **Bull case (for this report's ideas):** NZD/USD extends toward its second target (0.5820); AUD/NZD's stalled pullback resumes toward 1.1950 as the RBNZ/China-CPI theses continue to work; BoJ/MOF rhetoric hardens further or an actual intervention lands, cooling USD/JPY. *Invalidated by:* a confirmed, sustained break of 163.50 in USD/JPY or 1.2250 in AUD/NZD.
- **Base case:** USD/JPY continues to hold near its highs into tomorrow's US CPI without a confirmed break; AUD/NZD continues to consolidate in the lower half of its entry zone without a fresh catalyst. *Invalidated by:* a decisive break in either pair's key level, or a surprise US CPI print that moves the dollar sharply.
- **Bear case (for this report's ideas):** The Iran/Hormuz situation escalates yet further, tomorrow's US CPI prints hot on a core basis, USD/JPY breaks above 163.50, and AUD/NZD reverses back toward its highs. *Invalidated by:* a confirmed de-escalation in Iran/Hormuz combined with a soft US CPI print.

sections.title: Key Theme Driving Everything Right Now
sections.raw:
1. **The Iran/Strait of Hormuz crisis escalated sharply over the weekend from a "ceasefire is over" declaration to a formal Iranian closure of the Strait and a US naval blockade with a 20% cargo toll.** Iran retaliated with strikes against Kuwait, Jordan, and Qatar; shipping through the Strait has fallen roughly 52% week-on-week; oil has surged further (Brent briefly above $81).
2. **NZD/USD has cleared its first published target, the clearest confirmed win in this report's tracker so far**, as the RBNZ's (New Zealand) 8 Jul hike continues to prove a durable, multi-session catalyst even against a broad-dollar-strength crosscurrent.
3. **USD/JPY's now four-plus-session failure to catch any safe-haven bid — even through a formal Strait closure and naval blockade — remains this crisis's single most striking cross-asset anomaly**, and the item most likely to produce an abrupt catch-up move if the market's read on it changes, with tomorrow's US CPI and bank earnings adding fresh two-way risk into the pair.

sections.title: Historical Parallel Watch
sections.raw: No strong historical parallel today, though the partial echo flagged in prior reports has sharpened further. The Iran/Strait of Hormuz escalation remains fundamentally a geopolitical/commodity shock with FX and rates as second-order effects, not a clean match for any of the four FX-positioning-specific archetypes. That said, the market's weeks-long treatment of the Strait-reopening ceasefire as a durable, near-"guaranteed" state of affairs — the loose partial echo of Archetype 4 (complacent one-sided positioning around a "guaranteed" level) flagged in prior reports — has now been decisively broken by an actual formal closure, not just a rhetorical threat, sharpening that partial parallel meaningfully. It still isn't a clean match (there is no defended FX peg or rate level being tested, as in the SNB 2015 reference case), so this remains a partial echo rather than a genuine one.
